jess: Hey — running into a weird import error on Windows after installing redwood-sdk[async]. Fresh venv, Python 3.10.6. Steps: `python -m venv .venv` -> `.venv\\Scripts\\pip.exe install redwood-sdk[async]`. When I do `from redwood import Client` I get ImportError: cannot import name 'AsyncClient' from 'httpx'. Same package works on my Mac. Any ideas?

maya: Thanks — can you paste the output of `pip freeze` and `python -c \"import httpx, httpcore; print(httpx.__version__, httpcore.__version__)\"`? Also include the traceback if possible.

jess: pip freeze:
```
redwood-sdk==1.2.3
httpx==0.24.0
httpcore==0.16.0
typing-extensions==4.5.0
```
python -c output: `0.24.0 0.16.0`
traceback (short):
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "C:\\proj\\app\\main.py", line 1, in <module>
    from redwood import Client
  File "C:\\proj\\app\\.venv\\Lib\\site-packages\\redwood\\__init__.py", line 10, in <module>
    from httpx import AsyncClient
ImportError: cannot import name 'AsyncClient' from 'httpx' (C:\\proj\\app\\.venv\\Lib\\site-packages\\httpx\\__init__.py)
```

alex: Huh. AsyncClient is still part of httpx in 0.24, so this looks like an install/packaging shadowing issue rather than a runtime API change. Two quick checks: `pip check` and `python -c \"import httpx, inspect; print(httpx.__file__)\"` to see which httpx is being imported and whether there are leftover dist-info or egg-link files.

jess: Ran them — `pip check` shows `httpx 0.24.0 has requirement httpcore==0.16.*, but you have httpcore 0.16.0` (that's fine). The import path printed: `C:\\proj\\app\\.venv\\Lib\\site-packages\\httpx\\__init__.py`. But I also see a stray `httpx-0.23.3.dist-info` folder in site-packages (leftover from earlier dev work) and an `httpx.egg-link` pointing to `C:\\Users\\dev\\projects\\httpx-dev`. I think I had editable installs earlier.

maya: That explains it — egg-link/editable installs will shadow the installed wheel and can mismatch API surface. Try: `pip uninstall -y httpx httpcore` then remove the egg-link and any dangling `httpx-*.dist-info` dirs if present, then reinstall: `pip install redwood-sdk[async]` (or pin httpx to the version we test against).

alex: As a targeted quickfix, you can pin httpx to the known-good series we test against before reinstalling: `pip install 'httpx==0.23.*' 'httpcore==0.14.*'` then `pip install --force-reinstall redwood-sdk[async]`. Longer-term we'll add an integration test for editable-shadowing in CI and document the editable-dev caveat. I've added an issue for SDK packaging to clarify extras.

jess: I tried uninstalling, removed the egg-link, reinstalled with `pip install 'httpx==0.23.3'` then `pip install redwood-sdk[async]` and the import now succeeds. Thanks! Quick repro steps I used:
```
python -m venv .venv
.venv\\Scripts\\pip.exe uninstall -y httpx httpcore
# manually delete any httpx.egg-link and httpx-*.dist-info in site-packages
.venv\\Scripts\\pip.exe install 'httpx==0.23.3' 'httpcore==0.14.7'
.venv\\Scripts\\pip.exe install redwood-sdk[async]
python -c "from redwood import Client; print('ok')"
```

maya: Great — glad that worked. For support docs: avoid editable installs when testing SDK upgrades and prefer isolated venvs; if you must use a workspace httpx, use a clean venv for the app or pin transiently.

alex: Filed support ticket #SUP-412 and internal issue #SDK-789 to add a note to the Python SDK README about editable-shadowing and to tighten CI checks. Leaving a :thumbsup:.

maya: I'll follow up in the docs channel with the guide and a short checklist. Closing this thread — reopen if it recurs. :white_check_mark:
